reasoning: The extract commits to a further State Pension age review before the rise to 68 is legislated, and says it will use "the latest life expectancy projections" and evaluate "the effects of current rises in State Pension age". One line gives a timetable: the review is to be conducted by July 2023, and "will conclude by 2023". The extract gives a reason for evaluating, namely that the evaluation will "inform support mechanisms required for future increases" and "provide additional evidence to help the Government to assess the best course of action". It also names a loose scope: monitoring effects alongside reforms to the state and private pension systems, the welfare system and the labour market. That is more than a bare mention of evaluation, so it clears level 1 and reaches level 2 on plans and timetable. The strongest counter-example to level 2 is that the success measures are thin. No outcomes, indicators or methods are named, and testing or piloting is not discussed or ruled out. The only reference (42), benefit expenditure tables, is a spending figure and not an evaluation measure. Level 3 is not reached: nothing says what will happen to the results or whether they will be published, and impact assessments are mentioned only vaguely as being produced "at the appropriate time". To reach level 3 the document would need to name the outcomes to be measured, say whether the review will be published, and explain how its findings will feed into the decision. A motivated citizen cannot tell what would count as the policy working.
